## feature

<!-- new capability this task added -->

### pileup counts alleles on dense arrays per reference

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The port gives the same rows as the frozen per-base code on the full BAMs, on the 1 M-record subset and on random BAMs. One run alone on the full `all` BAM gave the timing.

#### description

```
type: [text, table]
```

1. `PileupStatsCollector` keeps the counts of one reference in numpy arrays: one row per position, one column per single-base allele.
2. One cached plan per `(record_pos, cs tag)` and per reference holds the parsed cs ops.
3. Reads that share a plan and carry no indel wait in a batch. A flush adds their quality sums per position.
4. A read with an insertion or a deletion applies at once when the counters at its anchor are positive. It applies after a flush otherwise.
5. The last passing substitution read in file order sets the `ref` base, as in the per-base code.

| Run of the `all` BAM (99,756,729 records) | Code | Wall-clock | CPU time | Max RSS | Rows |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| S34_1 rule, 2026-11-18 | 0.8.0 | 10,735 s | not recorded | not recorded | 18,003,654 |
| Investigation run A, 2026-11-25, load 13 to 26 | 0.9.0 | 13,186 s | 12,540.5 s | 11,946 MB | 18,003,654 |
| Port with the 0.9.0 quality index, 4 runs at one time | port | 2,802 s | 2,662.4 s | 5,280 MB | 18,003,654 |
| Port with the fixed index, alone, load 7 to 10 | port | 2,596 s | 2,500.0 s | 4,257 MB | 14,373,589 |

#### before

A pileup of the S34_1 `all` BAM took 2 h 59 min and 11.9 GB of memory. The per-base Python loop held 88 % of the time.

#### after

The same command takes 43 min and 4.3 GB on a loaded machine. With the 0.9.0 quality index it writes the same rows as before.

## fix

<!-- defect in the project or its artifacts, corrected this task -->

### pileup reads the quality of the counted base

```
level: high
```

#### reason

Three tests failed before the fix and pass after it. The index rule holds on 5,000 substitution bases of the real BAM. The fixed code equals the frozen per-base code with the same fix on the subset.

#### description

```
type: [text, table]
```

1. `tally_from_record` started `read_pos` at 0 (`src/sam_tagger/stats/pileup_stats.py:196` at 0.9.0), but QUAL holds the soft-clipped bases too.
2. So the filter tested the soft-clipped bases for the first aligned bases. For a `9S204M` read it tested the base 9 positions earlier for every other base.
3. SAM stores QUAL reverse-complemented for a `0x10` record. The filter tested the mirrored base of such a read.
4. The lookup now reverses QUAL for a reverse record and skips the leading soft clip (`src/sam_tagger/stats/pileup_dense.py`, `aligned_qualities`).

| `all` BAM, fixed index against 0.9.0 | 0.9.0 pileup | Fixed pileup |
|---|---|---|
| Rows | 18,003,654 | 14,373,589 |
| Reads on a non-reference allele | 22,192,079 | 14,511,660 |
| Mean `dp` per position | 2,182.46 | 2,182.06 |

5. The 3,649,942 rows that only the 0.9.0 pileup holds are 3,646,591 substitutions, 2,617 deletions and 1,134 insertions. Their median `ad` is 1.
6. Of 9,266,702 positions, `dp` is lower at 3,395,780, higher at 3,453,717 and unchanged at 2,417,205. The median change is 0.18 % of `dp`, the 90th percentile 1.27 %.
7. `ap_both.bam` behaves the same: 14,366,165 rows against 17,977,715, and 14,498,725 alt reads against 22,107,675.

#### before

The quality filter did not look at the base it counted. Low-quality error bases passed when a neighboring base had a good quality.

#### after

A base passes `--min-base-qual` when its own QUAL entry reaches the threshold. The S34_1 `all` pileup keeps about 80 % of its rows and 65 % of its alt reads.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text, statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

The three new tests before any fix (`.pixi/envs/dev/bin/python -m pytest -q tests/test_stats.py -k "quality_index or intervals_skip"`):

```text
E       assert [4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9, ...] == [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ...]
E         At index 0 diff: 4 != 1
E       assert [1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, ...] == [2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, ...]
E         At index 0 diff: 1 != 2
3 failed, 34 deselected in 0.61s
```

After the fix: `1 failed, 173 passed in 2.22s` (the BED test was still open).

Index rule on the real BAM (`annotated.bam`, substitution bases of forward reads, `seq[lead_soft + cs_offset] == alt`):

```text
substitution bases per strand [formula holds, fails]: {'fwd': [3000, 0], 'rev': [0, 0]}
records per strand in the first 3M: {'fwd': 3000000, 'rev': 0, 'other': 0}
```

`samtools view -c` on `annotated.bam`: `-f 16` gives `0`, `-F 16` gives `99756729`.

`out/all.diff.json` (`scripts/diff_outputs.py`, fixed against 0.9.0):

```json
{"rows_new": 14373589, "rows_old": 18003654, "rows_only_old": 3649942, "rows_only_new": 19877,
 "alt_reads_old": 22192079, "alt_reads_new": 14511660,
 "positions": 9266702, "dp_lower": 3395780, "dp_higher": 3453717, "dp_unchanged": 2417205,

```

:::

### BED intervals apply to substitutions and indels

```
level: high
```

#### reason

A test failed before the fix with the three extra rows and passes after it. The differential test covers BED files that cut through every op type.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The per-base code tested `position_in_intervals` for match runs only (`pileup_stats.py:209-212` at 0.9.0). The `*`, `+` and `-` ops had no test (`:225-298`).
2. `--intervals` reported a substitution outside the BED and an indel whose anchor lies outside.
3. Every op now tests its position. An indel tests its anchor.

#### before

A BED over the first 10 bases of a 30-base reference also reported a `+AC` row at position 12, a `-AC` row at position 15 and a `C` row at position 20.

#### after

The same BED reports positions 1 to 10 only.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`test_pileup_intervals_skip_substitution_and_indel_outside` before the fix:

```text
E       AssertionError: assert [(1, '.'), (2...(6, '.'), ...] == [(1, '.'), (2...(6, '.'), ...]
E         Left contains 3 more items, first extra item: (12, '+AC')
```

After the fix: `174 passed in 2.88s`.

:::

## assumption

<!-- unverified premise the work depends on -->

### the frozen oracle is the 0.9.0 algorithm with the two fixes

```
level: high
```

#### reason

`tests/pileup_oracle.py` differs from the committed file in the docstring, two imports, the class name, one line wrap and the appended record loop.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. `tests/pileup_oracle.py` is `git show 35f14ac:src/sam_tagger/stats/pileup_stats.py`, with the class renamed to `PileupOracle`.
2. `run_reference_pileup` in the same file repeats the `run_pileup` record loop of that commit.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`diff <(git show 35f14ac:src/sam_tagger/stats/pileup_stats.py) tests/pileup_oracle.py` reports 68 changed lines: lines 1 to 6 (docstring), the imports of `parse_bed` and `CS_REGEX`, line 98 (`class PileupOracle:`), the line wrap of a `logger.warning` call, and lines 363 to 410 (`run_reference_pileup`).

:::

### a positive counter at the anchor makes waiting reads irrelevant

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The rule follows from the three guards of the per-base code. The deep-coverage test and the fuzz runs hold the port against the oracle with both paths in use.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. A retro-fix decrement lowers the strand count, the total and `dp` of the anchor, each only when it is above 0.
2. Waiting batches hold increments only. They can change a guard only when the counter is 0.
3. So a read with an indel applies at once when `exists`, the strand count, the total and `dp` are positive at the anchor (`_pending_cannot_matter`). The collector flushes first otherwise.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic, text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Deep-coverage case (1,500 reads on two 60 bp references, 30 % error rate), one run:

```text
indel ops in the deep case: applied without a flush 1779 | after a flush 4
```

Fuzz of the reviewer (400 random BAMs with mutated cs tags, batch and plan-cache limits varied), `fuzz.py 0 400`:

```text
before the ref-order fix: tally: {'SAME': 394, 'DIFF': 6, 'RAISED': 0}
after the fixes:          tally: {'SAME': 400, 'DIFF': 0, 'RAISED': 0}
```

:::

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The machine carried a load average of 7 to 12 from other jobs during all runs. CPU time is less sensitive to that load than wall-clock, but the CPU frequency and the SMT siblings still move it.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The report gives CPU time and wall-clock of each run.
2. A ratio of two runs at one time is more reliable than a ratio against the 2026-11-18 run.

#### evidence

```

```

Load averages read during the work: `7.29 7.76 8.41`, `12.27 9.45 8.85`, `7.01 7.86 8.89`. `ps` showed a `qemu-system-x86` process of another user at 46.7 % CPU over 48 days.

:::

### the quality fix removes a third of the alt reads of S34_1

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The two full outputs of the `all` BAM differ in row count and in alt reads as stated. The cause is the index rule, shown by the tests and by the real-data check.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The 0.9.0 filter tested the quality of the base 9 positions earlier for a `9S204M` read. Most bases have a quality of 20 or more, so most error bases passed.
2. The fixed filter tests the error base itself. Alt reads fall from 22,192,079 to 14,511,660 on `annotated.bam`, and from 22,107,675 to 14,498,725 on `ap_both.bam`.
3. `dp` per position moves by a median of 0.18 %. The mean `dp` stays at 2,182.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

`out/all.diff.json`: `"alt_reads_old": 22192079, "alt_reads_new": 14511660`, `"relative_dp_change": {"median": 0.00178, "p90": 0.01269}`.

:::

## observation

<!-- what was noticed in data or behavior, without interpretation -->

### the record loop of the port costs more than the one of the prototype

```
level: medium
```

#### reason

The CPU time per record of the two full runs differs by 7.2 µs. The share of each cause is an estimate from the cProfile run on the subset, not a measurement on the full BAM.

#### description

```
type: [table]
```

| Item | Prototype of 2026-11-25 | Port |
|---|---|---|
| CPU time per record, full `all` BAM | 17.9 µs | 25.1 µs |
| Reads with an indel on the subset | 4 % | 4 % |
| Reads with an indel on the full BAM | 14.5 % | 14.5 % |
| Match update | one-hot block, contiguous slice adds | flat fancy indexing |
| cs warning and tag check per record | none | `_CsWatch.observe` and `has_tag` |

1. An indel read takes the single-read path. That path costs about 25 µs against about 17 µs in the prototype.
2. The port keeps the `_CsWatch` warning and the `has_tag` check of the product. The prototype had neither.

#### evidence

```
level: medium
type: [text]
```

Micro-benchmark of the match update on arrays of 204 positions and 8 slots, load about 8 (`np` 2.5.5):

```text

flat 1-D fancy (index built per call)     9.13 us
block: one-hot x total, slice adds       12.62 us
fancy single read (mask)                 21.01 us
block single read (mask)                 13.00 us
```

:::

### the independent review found one exactness hole in the port

```
level: high
```

#### reason

The reviewer reproduced the hole with two reads and confirmed the fix by a second fuzz run.

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The review ran 164 targeted cases, 800 random BAMs (400 with cs tags mutated against the CIGAR) and 300 runs with small batches.
2. Counts, `dp` and row order were identical in every run.
3. Two substitution reads with different cs reference letters at one position gave a different `ref`: the per-base code lets the last passing read in file order win, and the batches applied in plan order.
4. The review also found one new pyright error in the uncommitted file. The CI step `pixi run -e dev typecheck` would have failed.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Reviewer summary, `[MEDIUM] ref differs when two SNP ops carry different reference chars at one position — CONFIRMED. Input: reads *Tg, *Ag, *Tg at POS 6. Oracle gives ref=T, dense gives ref=A. Counts are equal.`

Reviewer summary, `[HIGH] New pyright error fails the CI typecheck step — CONFIRMED. pyright reports "Object of type None is not subscriptable" on flat[hit].`

:::

## process

<!-- audit of a significant action or decision between plan and report -->

### chose a flush before every indel read

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The first port flushed all waiting batches before each read with an indel.
2. On real data every 25th read has an indel, so a batch held about 6 reads and the flush cost dominated.
3. The counter rule of `_pending_cannot_matter` replaced the flush. The better action was to compute the batch size from the indel rate before the first design.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [statistic]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

Subset CPU time: 33.3 s with the flush rule, 24.2 s with the counter rule, 21.4 s with flat indexes, 23.3 s with the final code.

:::

### padded a short QUAL with zero bytes

```
status: wrong
```

#### description

```
type: [text]
```

1. The port pads a QUAL that is shorter than the cs tag with zero bytes.
2. With `--min-base-qual 0` a zero passes, so bases without a quality were counted.
3. The differential test found it (8 of 41 cases failed). The flush now masks the padded bases.

#### evidence

```
level: high
type: [text]
```

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}

```text
E       AssertionError: DataFrames are different (height (row count) mismatch)
E       [left]: 268
E       [right]: 267
8 failed, 203 passed in 4.72s
```

:::

type: [text]
